intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges and trails. Walk at canopy level to observe exotic birds, howler monkeys, and tropical flora up close. The dramatic backdrop of the active volcano makes this one of Costa Rica's most scenic eco-adventures.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas along jungle trails that open onto pristine Pacific beaches. The guide's telescope brings hidden wildlife into stunning close-up detail.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition & Night Walk
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado, dubbed by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. A full-day guided expedition covers primary rainforest trails where tapirs, peccaries, jaguars, and harpy eagles have been spotted. Cap the day with a guided night walk to discover nocturnal creatures like tree frogs, tarantulas, and kinkajous.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency or withdraw colones from airport ATM, and arrange budget shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (shared shuttle ~$15–25 USD vs private taxi ~$60). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the local beach at sunset to spot shore birds and possibly sea turtles. Explore the nearest town center on foot to scout local sodas (traditional Costa Rican diners) and budget eateries for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport — gallo pinto (rice and beans) at an airport café (~$5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before departure
meals.dinner: Find a local soda near the resort — try casado (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and protein) for ~$5–8 USD. Ask hotel staff for their top budget recommendation.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and acclimatization. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and ask hotel reception about reputable local tour operators for best budget rates. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny, warm weather (~28–32°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and nearby coastal trail. Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, coatis, and iguanas. Bring binoculars if available. This is free and one of the best times to spot wildlife before the heat of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (e.g., Manuel Antonio or Tortuguero depending on resort location). Purchase entrance ticket (~$18–20 USD) and explore marked trails independently without a guide to save money. Spot sloths, capuchin monkeys, toucans, and diverse reptiles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a relaxing swim at golden hour. Walk to a local market or small grocery store to pick up snacks and water for upcoming days — buying water and fruit locally saves significant money.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or visit a local bakery/soda for gallo pinto with eggs and coffee (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local mini-super before entering the park — buy bread, local cheese, fruit, and juice (~$4–5 USD total)
meals.dinner: Beachside soda dinner — try arroz con pollo (chicken with rice) or fish fillet with patacones (fried plantains) for ~$7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the national park early (opens at 7:00 AM) to beat the crowds and maximize wildlife sightings. Wear light, neutral-colored clothing and bring insect repellent and sunscreen. Stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining tour through a local operator (shop around — group rates can be ~$45–65 USD vs premium operators at $100+). Most tours include 8–12 platforms through the rainforest canopy with views of the jungle and wildlife. Depart early for the zip-line site.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby hanging bridges or canopy walkway if included in the tour package, or pay a small separate fee (~$15–20 USD). Walk through the cloud forest or rainforest at canopy level — excellent for spotting toucans, morpho butterflies, and sloths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Relax and recover. Visit the town center for a budget dinner and explore local artisan stalls for affordable souvenirs (haggle respectfully).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a local soda before the tour — gallo pinto, fruit, and coffee (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Many zip-line operators include a basic lunch — confirm when booking. If not, eat at a local soda near the tour site (~$6–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Try a local pizza or pasta spot for variety, or a Chinese-Costa Rican fusion restaurant (very common and budget-friendly) for ~$6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1 day in advance. Wear closed-toe shoes and secure any loose items. Most reputable operators provide helmets and harnesses. Avoid the cheapest unlicensed operators — look for ICT (Costa Rica Tourism Board) certified companies.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget boat tour or kayak rental along a nearby river or estuary to spot crocodiles, caimans, herons, kingfishers, and river otters. Group boat tours can cost as little as $20–35 USD per person. Alternatively, rent a kayak independently for ~$15–20 USD for a half-day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall hike — many are accessible with just a small entrance fee ($2–5 USD) or free. Swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. These are often less crowded than main national parks and equally stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in town if available (check local boards). Otherwise, enjoy a sunset on the beach and watch for nesting sea turtles (February is nesting season in some areas).

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and toast at a local café (~$3–5 USD) — look for places serving fresh tropical fruits like papaya, mango, and pineapple
meals.lunch: Eat at a local soda near the waterfall or river area — casado or rice and beans with fish (~$6–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal if the hotel has kitchen facilities, or buy fresh fruit, bread, and local cheese from a grocery store for a light budget dinner (~$5–7 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: For the boat tour, early morning departures (6:00–7:00 AM) offer the best wildlife activity. Bring waterproof bags for electronics. The waterfall hike may require sturdy shoes — trails can be muddy even in dry season.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure: Take a shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby volcano or cloud forest reserve (e.g., Arenal, Poás, or Monteverde depending on location). Local buses are extremely affordable (~$2–8 USD each way). Depart by 7:00 AM to maximize time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the volcano or cloud forest trails. Look for resplendent quetzals (in cloud forest), poison dart frogs, and exotic orchids. Many volcanic areas also offer free or low-cost hot spring rivers (natural, not resort pools) — ask locals for directions.
day_by_day.evening: Begin return journey or overnight in a budget hostel near the volcano/cloud forest area (~$12–18 USD per night in a dorm) to avoid a rushed return.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — buy packed snacks and fruit from a local market the night before to save time and money
meals.lunch: Eat at a soda near the park entrance — set lunch menus (casado) are typically $5–8 USD and very filling
meals.dinner: If staying overnight, find a local soda or budget restaurant near the hostel (~$7–10 USD). If returning, grab dinner at a roadside soda on the way back.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day. Confirm bus schedules the day before — local Tico buses run on their own schedule. Bring layers if visiting cloud forest (Monteverde can be cool and misty even in February). A day trip to Arenal from the coast is long but doable.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighted near the volcano/cloud forest: Morning wildlife walk before returning. If returned to resort: Rest morning — enjoy the beach, swim, and relax. This is a planned rest day to recover from Day 5's long journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary near the resort area. These are typically small, affordable attractions (~$10–15 USD) with guided tours included in the price. Excellent for close-up wildlife photography.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk. Join a free guided stargazing session if offered by the hotel, or simply enjoy the night sky on the beach. February in Costa Rica offers excellent clear skies in the dry season.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local soda — try chorreado (corn pancakes) with sour cream and coffee, a traditional Costa Rican breakfast (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Beach-side lunch at a local chiringuito (beach shack) — ceviche and patacones with fresh limeade (~$7–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly tonight — find a mid-range local seafood restaurant and try fresh grilled fish (pargo or corvina) with rice and salad (~$12–15 USD). Still very affordable by international standards.

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally relaxed. Use this time to do laundry (many hostels/budget hotels have coin laundry or hand-wash facilities), recharge devices, review remaining days, and book any outstanding tours. Stay hydrated — the dry season heat can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided wildlife photography walk led by a local naturalist guide. Look for budget community-run tours (~$20–30 USD) rather than large commercial operators. These walks focus on finding sloths, monkeys, toucans, and reptiles in local forests and gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or cacao plantation for a self-guided or budget tour (~$10–15 USD). Learn about sustainable agriculture, taste fresh cacao, and understand Costa Rica's eco-conscious farming culture — directly tied to the eco-adventure theme.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in a nearby forest or reserve to spot nocturnal wildlife — red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, night herons, and insects. Many local guides offer budget night walks for ~$20–25 USD per person.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh orange juice at a local soda (~$4–5 USD)
meals.lunch: On-farm lunch if offered by the cacao tour (often included or available for ~$8–10 USD) — typically features fresh local produce
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the night walk — rice and beans with vegetables at a local soda (~$5–7 USD). Eat early to be comfortable during the walk.

day_by_day.notes: For the night walk, wear dark or neutral clothing and bring a red-light headlamp (red light is less disruptive to nocturnal animals than white light). Closed-toe shoes are essential. Book the night walk in advance as spots are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day white-water rafting excursion on a nearby river (e.g., Río Savegre or Río Pacuare depending on location). Look for Class II–III beginner-friendly options for a lower cost (~$45–65 USD for a half-day with equipment and guide). This is one of Costa Rica's premier eco-adventure activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue rafting or, if half-day tour, return to resort and visit a nearby lagoon or mangrove forest for a self-guided walk. Mangroves are free to explore and home to diverse bird species, crabs, and fish.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the adventure day with a local cerveza (beer) and snacks at a beach bar. Watch the sunset and share stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before rafting — eggs, gallo pinto, fruit, and coffee (~$5–7 USD). Eat at least 1.5 hours before the activity.
meals.lunch: Most rafting operators include a riverside lunch — confirm when booking. Typically fresh fruit, sandwiches, and water.
meals.dinner: Local soda dinner — try sopa negra (black bean soup) or olla de carne (beef stew) for a hearty, authentic, and affordable meal (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm swimming ability requirements with the rafting operator beforehand. Life jackets and helmets are always provided. Bring a change of dry clothes and secure valuables in a waterproof bag. Avoid rafting immediately after heavy rain as river levels can become dangerous.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby indigenous community or cultural center for a guided cultural tour (~$15–25 USD). Learn about Bribri or Boruca indigenous traditions, medicinal plants, and traditional crafts. This supports local communities directly and offers a unique perspective beyond typical tourist experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local beach that is less frequented by tourists — ask hotel staff for recommendations. Snorkel if gear is available to rent (~$10–15 USD) to spot tropical fish, rays, and possibly sea turtles underwater.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free salsa or merengue class if offered at a local bar or community center — a fun and authentic way to engage with Costa Rican culture. Many beach towns have free or low-cost dance nights.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit bowl and granola at a local café (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat at the indigenous community if a meal is offered (often included in cultural tour cost or available for ~$5–8 USD) — try traditional dishes made with yuca, plantain, and local game
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner at a local soda — try fresh ceviche with tostadas and a fresh coconut water (~$8–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting indigenous communities, always ask permission before photographing people. Purchase handicrafts directly from artisans to ensure fair compensation. Bring cash as card payments are rarely accepted in small communities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching session — Costa Rica has over 900 bird species. Hire a local birding guide for a 3-hour walk (~$20–30 USD) or join a free birding group through the hotel. Target species: scarlet macaw, toucan, motmot, and tanagers. Bring binoculars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby sea turtle conservation project or wildlife rescue center (~$10–20 USD entrance). Interact with rescued sloths, monkeys, and birds in a responsible, ethical setting. Many centers also allow volunteer opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Guided sea turtle nesting observation tour on the beach (February is nesting season in some Costa Rican beaches). Book through a certified operator (~$25–35 USD) — only certified guides are legally permitted to lead these tours to protect the turtles.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before birdwatching — pack a banana and granola bar from the hotel or a local shop (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Post-birdwatching meal at a local soda — try a big casado with fresh juice (~$7–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the turtle tour — rice and beans with avocado and a fruit smoothie (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The sea turtle tour requires strict red-light-only rules and silence on the beach. No flash photography. Tours typically depart after 8:00 PM and can run until midnight depending on turtle activity. Dress in dark clothing and bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared shuttle to a different nearby beach or coastal town for a change of scenery (~$2–5 USD bus fare). Explore the town market, browse local artisan stalls, and pick up affordable souvenirs — look for handmade jewelry, painted wood carvings, and coffee products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle in the new town (~$8–12 USD for half-day) and cycle along coastal paths or through a nearby forest trail. This is a fantastic low-cost way to cover ground and spot wildlife at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Spend the evening reviewing photos and journaling. Visit a local bar for a farewell-style drink with fellow travelers met during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure (~$4–6 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Explore the new town's sodas and try something different — maybe a Caribbean-style rice and beans cooked in coconut milk if near the Caribbean coast (~$6–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Back at the resort area — find a local spot and try lomito (tenderloin) or pollo a la plancha (grilled chicken) with salad (~$9–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep bus ticket receipts for budget tracking. If cycling, check the bike condition before renting — test brakes and tires. Cycling in the midday heat can be exhausting — bring plenty of water and wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Final eco-adventure activity: Book a guided mangrove kayaking tour (~$30–45 USD) through a local operator. Paddle through mangrove tunnels spotting crocodiles, monkeys, tropical birds, and exotic fish. This is a peaceful yet thrilling finale to the eco-adventure theme of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon on the beach. Swim, sunbathe, and reflect on the trip. This is also a good time to pack, organize luggage, and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer local restaurant. Try a traditional Costa Rican feast: fresh seafood platter, fried yuca, patacones, and a local craft beer or fresh agua dulce (hot sugarcane drink). Budget ~$15–20 USD for a special send-off meal.

meals.breakfast: Local soda breakfast — enjoy one last gallo pinto with eggs, natilla, and strong Costa Rican coffee (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh ceviche, tostadas, and a cold coconut water (~$7–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant — fresh grilled fish or shrimp with all the trimmings (~$15–20 USD). Still budget-friendly by global standards.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics tonight — shuttle or taxi to the airport, flight check-in time, and any airport fees. Exchange remaining colones back to your home currency or spend them on last-minute airport souvenirs. Keep some colones for airport food and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — take in the sounds of howler monkeys, the sight of pelicans diving for fish, and the warmth of the Costa Rican sun one last time. Collect a small piece of driftwood or a shell as a free natural souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard check-out 11:00–12:00). Arrange shared shuttle to Juan Santamaría International Airport (~$15–25 USD). Arrive at airport 2–3 hours before international flight departure. Browse duty-free for last-minute coffee or chocolate gifts (Costa Rican coffee makes an excellent affordable souvenir).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica. Reflect on 13 incredible days of eco-adventure, zip-lining, wildlife encounters, and authentic cultural experiences — all on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a quick soda breakfast near the hotel before checkout (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch — use remaining colones at an airport café or soda (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-managed 13-day Costa Rica budget trip should cost approximately $800–1,200 USD per person (excluding flights) covering accommodation, meals, transport, and activities. Always tip local guides 10–15% — it makes a significant difference to their income. Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges and trails. Walk at canopy level to observe exotic birds, howler monkeys, and tropical flora up close. The dramatic backdrop of the active volcano makes this one of Costa Rica's most scenic eco-adventures.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the scenic drive and first glimpses of Costa Rica's lush landscapes. Check in, freshen up, and explore the beachfront resort grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beach at sunset to decompress from travel. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the resort bar. Light orientation walk around the nearby town to get your bearings and pick up any essentials.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport – try a traditional 'casado' (rice, beans, protein) at an airport café (~$10–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant – fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and a local Imperial beer (~$20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very relaxed. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings at the resort's concierge desk. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones for small purchases. Stay hydrated – the tropical climate can be intense after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided sunrise wildlife walk along the beach and adjacent mangrove estuary. Look for scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and coastal birds with a local naturalist guide (~$35–45 per person, 2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby national park or wildlife refuge for a self-guided or guided rainforest hike. Spot sloths, iguanas, and tropical birds. Visit a local butterfly garden or reptile sanctuary (~$15–20 entrance).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a swim in the pool or ocean. Attend an optional resort-run 'Introduction to Costa Rica's Biodiversity' talk if available. Relax and prepare for the adventure-heavy days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh juice (~$12–15 included or add-on)
meals.lunch: Soda (local family restaurant) near the park – casado with chicken or fish (~$8–10)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant in town – grilled sea bass with plantains and a salad (~$18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing and sturdy closed-toe shoes for the hike. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and insect repellent. Binoculars are highly recommended for wildlife spotting.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Depart early by shuttle to Arenal Volcano area (travel time varies by resort location, typically 2–4 hours). Check in to a day-use arrangement or simply store bags and head straight to the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike. Trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges with sweeping views of the volcano (~$28–35 self-guided, $55–70 guided).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the hanging bridges loop trail in the afternoon. Keep eyes peeled for toucans, poison dart frogs, coatis, and sloths in the forest canopy. Visit the Arenal Volcano National Park viewpoint for dramatic volcano photos.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous La Fortuna hot springs (Baldi or Titokú Hot Springs recommended for mid-range budget, ~$35–45). Enjoy the therapeutic volcanic mineral waters surrounded by jungle at night – a truly magical Costa Rican experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure – grab a to-go pack if needed
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a local soda in La Fortuna town – rice, beans, and grilled chicken (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a La Fortuna restaurant such as Don Rufino or Restaurante Nene's – try the heart of palm salad and beef tenderloin (~$20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day – wear comfortable hiking shoes with ankle support. Bring a rain jacket as the Arenal area receives frequent afternoon showers. Bring a dry bag for electronics. Overnight stay in La Fortuna is optional and recommended if budget allows (budget $60–100/night for a mid-range lodge) to avoid long return drive.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in La Fortuna (or return from resort). Optional: La Fortuna Waterfall hike – descend 500+ steps to a stunning 70-meter waterfall and swim in the natural pool below (~$18 entrance fee). Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal with a local outfitter (~$40–55 for 2 hours). Enjoy panoramic views of the volcano reflected in the lake. Alternatively, visit the Arenal Eco Zoo or local wildlife rescue center.
day_by_day.evening: Return shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort or a local restaurant. Rest and recover from two active days.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Fortuna hotel or local café – gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh coffee (~$8–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the waterfall or at a lakeside soda (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby local eatery – grilled chicken with rice, beans, and fried plantains (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: The La Fortuna Waterfall steps are steep and can be slippery – use the rope handrails. Water shoes are ideal for swimming. If staying at the resort, confirm the shuttle schedule back in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Depart early for Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3–4 hours from Arenal via scenic lake crossing ferry or road). Arrive and check in for the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – soar through the misty cloud forest on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits with over 10 platforms, Tarzan swings, and a rappel (~$55–75 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-line tour, explore the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve on foot. Walk trails through primary cloud forest searching for the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and howler monkeys. Hire a local guide for best wildlife sightings (~$20–25 for 2-hour guided walk).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde town of Santa Elena. Browse artisan shops and local galleries. Attend the optional 'Night Walk' guided tour through the cloud forest to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tarantulas, and glass frogs (~$25–35).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort or packed snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Café in Santa Elena – try a traditional empanada and fresh-squeezed lemonade (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant or Sabor Tico in Santa Elena – local cuisine with a view (~$18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde is cooler and windier than the coast – bring a light fleece or jacket. Cloud forest weather is unpredictable; always carry a rain layer. Book the zip-line tour in advance, especially in February (peak season). Overnight in Monteverde strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided bird-watching walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve. February is excellent for spotting the resplendent quetzal during nesting season. A specialist birding guide dramatically increases sighting success (~$30–45 for 3-hour tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery – walk through enclosed gardens with hundreds of tropical butterfly species and photograph hummingbirds feeding just inches away (~$15). Stop at the Cheese Factory (La Lechería) – a local institution since 1953, offering dairy products and light meals.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort (3–4 hours). Enjoy a relaxing evening at the beach. Sunset swim and a quiet dinner to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Monteverde – fresh fruit, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee (~$10–14)
meals.lunch: La Lechería Cheese Factory – cheese platter, fresh bread, and local produce (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or beachside soda – seafood platter with tropical salad (~$18–24)

day_by_day.notes: The road from Monteverde can be rough and unpaved in sections – a 4WD vehicle or organized shuttle is recommended. Confirm shuttle booking the evening before. The quetzal is most active between 6–9 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Morning yoga session on the beach (check if the resort offers classes) or gentle stretching after the active past few days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach day at the resort. Swim, snorkel in the near-shore reef (if available), or rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort (~$15–20/hour). Alternatively, book a local surf lesson for beginners (~$45–60 including board and instructor).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the beach bar. Explore the local town's Saturday/Sunday market if available – pick up local crafts, fresh fruit, and artisan goods. Casual dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – enjoy every item on the buffet as a reward for the week's adventures (~$12–15)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar – ceviche tostadas, fresh coconut water, and tropical fruit (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Local town restaurant – wood-fired pizza or fresh seafood pasta (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your mid-trip rest day – don't skip it! Active travel in Costa Rica's heat and humidity is physically demanding. Use this day to do laundry, recharge electronics, review the second week's bookings, and apply any sunburn treatment needed.

day_by_day.morning: Guided mangrove kayaking tour through a nearby estuary or river delta. Paddle through a cathedral of mangrove roots while spotting crocodiles, caimans, herons, and roseate spoonbills with a naturalist guide (~$45–65 for 3-hour tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center. Learn about Costa Rica's conservation efforts and get close to animals including toucans, sloths, monkeys, and peccaries that are being rehabilitated for release (~$15–20 entrance).
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class with a local Costa Rican family or chef – learn to make traditional dishes like gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake (~$55–75 per person including dinner). A fantastic cultural immersion experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local bakery – fresh pan dulce and café chorreado (traditional Costa Rican drip coffee) (~$6–10)
meals.lunch: Soda near the rescue center – casado with fresh lemonade (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Included in the cooking class – eat what you make! (~$55–75 covers the experience and meal)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance as spots fill quickly. The mangrove tour is best done in the morning when wildlife is most active and temperatures are cooler. Bring water shoes for the kayaking tour.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a nearby national park or protected area (such as Manuel Antonio, Corcovado day trip, or Tortuguero depending on resort location). Morning guided rainforest hike with a certified naturalist – spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and Jesus Christ lizards (~$45–65 guided entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach time within the national park (if applicable – Manuel Antonio has stunning park beaches). Snorkel off the park's rocky points to see colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and rays. Pack out all trash and follow Leave No Trace principles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Optional: visit a local rancho-style restaurant for a traditional 'Tico' dinner with live marimba music.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure (~$12–15)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort or purchased at park entrance – sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Rancho-style local restaurant – whole fried snapper with patacones (fried plantains), rice, and salad (~$18–25)

day_by_day.notes: National park entrance must be reserved online in advance (especially Manuel Antonio which has a daily visitor cap). Bring biodegradable sunscreen and insect repellent. No plastic bags allowed in most national parks.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on a nearby river (Class II–III suitable for most fitness levels, Class IV available for thrill-seekers). A full-morning rafting adventure through jungle gorges with experienced guides (~$65–85 per person including equipment and safety briefing).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local coffee or chocolate (cacao) plantation for a guided tour and tasting. Learn about the bean-to-bar or seed-to-cup process and sample fresh Costa Rican chocolate or coffee products (~$25–35 including tastings).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy the pool, get a massage at the resort spa (~$60–80 for 60 minutes), or attend a resort-hosted cultural presentation on Costa Rican wildlife and conservation.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before rafting – banana, granola bar, and coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch provided by the outfitter or at a local soda – hearty casado to replenish energy (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – try the 'surf and turf' special or fresh catch of the day (~$22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear a swimsuit under quick-dry clothes for rafting. Leave valuables at the resort – most outfitters provide waterproof bags for phones. The chocolate/coffee tour is a wonderful afternoon activity that's easy on the body after a physical morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sea kayaking or snorkeling boat tour to offshore islands or rocky outcrops. Look for sea turtles, dolphins, manta rays, and abundant reef fish. Many operators offer combo snorkel-kayak tours (~$55–75 per person including equipment).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local indigenous community or cultural center to learn about the Bribri or Boruca people's traditions, medicinal plants, and ancestral relationship with the rainforest (~$30–45 for a guided community tour). Purchase authentic handmade crafts directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sailing cruise along the coast – enjoy appetizers, tropical drinks, and spectacular Pacific sunset views from the water (~$55–75 per person). One of the most memorable Costa Rica experiences.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – fuel up for the water activities (~$12–15)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside restaurant – shrimp tacos and fresh coconut water (~$12–16)
meals.dinner: Appetizers and drinks included on the sunset cruise; supplement with a light late dinner at the resort bar (~$10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset sailing cruise at least 2 days in advance. February is peak dry season on the Pacific coast – expect calm seas and stunning sunsets. Apply seasickness patches behind the ear the night before if prone to motion sickness.

day_by_day.morning: Final big adventure day: Horseback riding through tropical countryside to a hidden waterfall. A 3–4 hour guided ride through farmland, river crossings, and forest with a swim at the destination waterfall (~$55–75 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from horseback riding and enjoy a final afternoon at the resort beach. Swim, lounge in a hammock, and soak in the last full day of Costa Rica's paradise. Optional: final snorkel session or stand-up paddleboard.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the best restaurant in the area. Splurge slightly on this final evening – try a multi-course meal featuring local ingredients: hearts of palm salad, sea bass ceviche, and a classic tres leches dessert. Toast to an incredible trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – enjoy the full spread one more time (~$12–15)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the beach or resort – ceviche and fresh fruit plate (~$12–16)
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant or resort's finest dining option – full multi-course Costa Rican feast (~$35–50 per person, splurge-worthy finale)

day_by_day.notes: Horseback riding requires closed-toe shoes or boots – most operators provide helmets. Let the guide know your riding experience level. Pack and organize luggage in the evening to make the final morning stress-free. Keep out only what you need for the last day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach – take it all in one last time. Pack remaining items and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange airport transfer (book in advance – allow 3–4 hours for transfer plus check-in buffer depending on resort location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport transfer and departure. If time permits before the flight, browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Costa Rican souvenirs: coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and local artwork. Clear immigration and customs early.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of eco-adventure, zip-lining through cloud forests, wildlife encounters, volcanic hot springs, and beachside bliss in one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or grab fresh fruit and coffee from a local bakery near the resort (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant – a final gallo pinto or casado before departure (~$12–18)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at a layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and work backwards to calculate when to leave the resort. Costa Rica's airports recommend arriving 3 hours early for international flights. Don't forget to declare any agricultural products – most packaged coffee and chocolate is fine. Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges and trails. Walk at canopy level to observe exotic birds, howler monkeys, and tropical flora up close. The dramatic backdrop of the active volcano makes this one of Costa Rica's most scenic eco-adventures.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas along jungle trails that open onto pristine Pacific beaches. The guide's telescope brings hidden wildlife into stunning close-up detail.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition & Night Walk
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado, dubbed by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. A full-day guided expedition covers primary rainforest trails where tapirs, peccaries, jaguars, and harpy eagles have been spotted. Cap the day with a guided night walk to discover nocturnal creatures like tree frogs, tarantulas, and kinkajous.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Juan Santamaría International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort arranged with a dedicated concierge meet-and-greet at arrivals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort orientation and welcome amenities. Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a curated welcome cocktail and fresh tropical fruit platter prepared by the resort. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the resort's oceanfront terrace. Light exploration of resort grounds, spa preview, and early dinner to adjust to local time.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light bites and tropical welcome spread arranged by the resort upon arrival — fresh ceviche, plantain chips, and local fruit selections
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant — recommended: grilled pargo (red snapper) with hearts of palm salad, paired with a Costa Rican craft beer or local Guanacaste wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-confirmed. Request early room preparation with the resort so the suite is ready upon arrival. Keep Day 1 relaxed to allow for jet lag adjustment. Tip: request a beachside cabana setup for the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Luxurious resort morning — early sunrise yoga session on the private beach offered by the resort's wellness team, followed by a full gourmet breakfast at the ocean-view dining terrace. Explore the resort's private nature trail along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling or kayaking excursion arranged through the resort's water sports concierge along the pristine coastal waters. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's infinity pool with a dedicated poolside butler service and curated tropical cocktail menu.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's clifftop bar. Enjoy a private stargazing experience on the beach arranged by the resort with a local astronomer guide.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — freshly squeezed guanábana juice, gallo pinto with farm eggs, tropical fruit platters, and artisan Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside or beachside private dining — lobster tacos, fresh ceviche trio, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the resort — multi-course tasting menu featuring local ingredients such as heart of palm, sea bass, and plantain-crusted chicken, with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fully acclimatize and enjoy the resort's premium amenities. Book the chef's table experience in advance as it typically requires a reservation. Confirm water sports availability with the concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Depart resort by private luxury vehicle for Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 2–3 hours depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour with a certified naturalist guide at park opening. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and coatis in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided wildlife tour through Manuel Antonio's lush trails leading to the iconic Playa Espadilla Sur and Playa Manuel Antonio. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the resort packed in a premium cooler. Swim in the calm turquoise waters of Playa Manuel Antonio after the tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort or check into a luxury lodge near Manuel Antonio (if multi-destination trip structure applies). Relax and review wildlife photos from the day.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — avocado toast with local cheese, tropical smoothie, and Costa Rican espresso
meals.lunch: Premium private picnic prepared by the resort's kitchen — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, local cheeses, and sparkling water, enjoyed on the beach at Manuel Antonio
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Cantina or Emilio's Café near Manuel Antonio — renowned for fresh seafood, grilled lobster, and local casado platters in a lush jungle-view setting

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — book the guided tour well in advance. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing and waterproof footwear. Bring biodegradable sunscreen and insect repellent. Binoculars are essential and may be provided by the guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight or luxury ground transfer to the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region (approximately 45 minutes by charter plane). Begin the Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition — venture deep into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Morning hike with an expert naturalist guide through primary rainforest teeming with tapirs, jaguars (rare sighting), scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition along remote jungle trails. Visit pristine jungle waterfalls and hidden river crossings. Observe nesting seabirds and marine life along the park's coastal sections. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch in a jungle clearing.
day_by_day.evening: Corcovado National Park Night Walk — experience the jungle after dark with a guided torch-lit walk. Encounter nocturnal species including red-eyed tree frogs, fer-de-lance snakes, tapirs, peccaries, and bioluminescent fungi. Return to luxury eco-lodge accommodation in the Osa Peninsula.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before transfer — fresh tropical fruits, granola, local yogurt, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle picnic prepared by the eco-lodge — organic sandwiches, tropical fruit, local snacks, and filtered water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the eco-lodge's open-air restaurant — farm-to-table cuisine featuring locally caught fish, organic vegetables, and homemade desserts under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits — ensure these are secured through your tour operator. The night walk is included as an extension of the day expedition. Wear long sleeves, long trousers, and sturdy waterproof hiking boots. The Osa Peninsula is remote — confirm all logistics including charter flight details in advance. Recommended luxury lodges: Lapa Rios or Bosque del Cabo.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at the Osa Peninsula eco-lodge for an early morning birdwatching session on the lodge's private forest trails — spot toucans, hummingbirds, and scarlet macaws at dawn. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the lodge's treetop restaurant overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private dolphin and whale-watching boat tour departing from Drake Bay (the Osa Peninsula is one of the world's premier humpback whale watching destinations, especially in February). Snorkel at Caño Island Biological Reserve, a world-class dive site with sea turtles, sharks, and manta rays.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's clifftop terrace. Relaxed evening with a private massage at the lodge's jungle spa. Stargazing from the eco-lodge's private deck — the Osa Peninsula has virtually zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the lodge's treetop restaurant — eggs benedict with local herbs, fresh tropical juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch on the boat during the marine excursion — fresh ceviche, tropical fruits, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Private chef's dinner at the eco-lodge — whole grilled snapper caught that morning, organic salads, plantain gratin, and local chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: February is an excellent month for humpback whale sightings in the Osa Peninsula — confirm with the tour operator. Caño Island snorkeling requires a separate park permit. Book the jungle spa massage in advance. Pack a waterproof dry bag for the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from the Osa Peninsula to Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (approximately 1.5–2 hours via charter). Check into a luxury eco-lodge in Tortuguero — recommended: Tortuga Lodge & Gardens. Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide silently through the jungle canal network spotting caimans, river otters, manatees, green iguanas, and hundreds of bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat safari deeper into Tortuguero's waterway labyrinth. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about Tortuguero's world-famous sea turtle nesting programs. Explore the village of Tortuguero by foot — a small, charming Caribbean community accessible only by boat or plane.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury eco-lodge for sunset cocktails on the canal-view deck. Attend a guided evening presentation by the lodge's resident naturalist on Tortuguero's ecosystem and sea turtle conservation efforts.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Osa eco-lodge before charter flight — fresh fruits, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Tortuga Lodge — Caribbean-style rice and beans, grilled fish, fresh salad, and tropical juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Tortuga Lodge's elegant dining room — Caribbean-influenced cuisine featuring coconut shrimp, jerk-spiced chicken, and rum-infused desserts

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small aircraft — all logistics must be pre-arranged. February is the green sea turtle off-season for nesting, but leatherback turtles may begin arriving late February. Confirm turtle activity with the lodge. The canal boat safari is best in early morning or late afternoon for optimal wildlife sightings. Mosquito repellent is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn guided sea turtle patrol on Tortuguero Beach with a certified guide — February marks the early arrival of leatherback sea turtles, offering a rare and extraordinary wildlife encounter. Return to lodge for a full gourmet breakfast. Second morning boat safari focusing on bird species — Tortuguero hosts over 300 bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through Tortuguero's narrower jungle canals — a more intimate wildlife experience than motorized boat tours. Spot poison dart frogs, Jesus Christ lizards, and nesting kingfishers from the water level. Afternoon relaxation at the lodge's pool surrounded by tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Tortuga Lodge's premier dining experience. Sunset cocktail cruise on a private boat along the main Tortuguero canal.

meals.breakfast: Post-turtle patrol breakfast at the lodge — hearty gallo pinto, fresh eggs, tropical fruits, and strong Caribbean coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at the lodge — fresh ceviche, Caribbean patacones (fried plantains), and chilled agua de pipa (fresh coconut water)
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at Tortuga Lodge — lobster thermidor, Caribbean-style whole fish, chocolate lava cake with local cacao, and premium rum selection

day_by_day.notes: The pre-dawn turtle patrol requires advance booking through the lodge and Sea Turtle Conservancy. Strict red-light-only rules apply on the beach — no flash photography. Kayak rentals or guided kayak tours should be reserved the night before. This is a full, immersive day — pace yourself appropriately.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat transfer from Tortuguero to Limón, then luxury ground transfer to the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours with scenic stops). Stop at a local Caribbean bakery in Limón for traditional pan bon (Caribbean sweet bread) and fresh fruit. Arrive at Arenal and check into a luxury volcano-view lodge — recommended: The Springs Resort & Spa or Nayara Springs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike — trek through lush primary and secondary rainforest on a network of hanging suspension bridges offering aerial views of the rainforest canopy. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and coatis along the trail. The hanging bridges provide spectacular views of Arenal Volcano on clear days.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the luxury thermal hot springs at the resort — Arenal's volcanic geothermal activity feeds natural mineral-rich hot springs. Enjoy a private couples' hot spring experience or a full spa treatment at the resort's volcanic-inspired wellness center.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tortuga Lodge before departure — tropical fruits, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a scenic restaurant en route to Arenal or at the hanging bridges visitor center — recommended: El Novillo del Arenal for premium grilled meats with volcano views
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — wood-fired meats, local heart of palm salad, and artisan desserts with Arenal Volcano as the dramatic backdrop

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Tortuguero to Arenal is long but scenic — arrange a comfortable luxury vehicle with a knowledgeable driver-guide. The hanging bridges are best visited in the afternoon when wildlife activity increases. Book the private hot spring experience at the resort in advance. Arenal Volcano is most visible in the early morning before clouds gather.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wake-up for the best Arenal Volcano views before clouds roll in — enjoy coffee on your private villa balcony or terrace. Guided birdwatching walk on the resort's private trails — Arenal is home to over 500 bird species including the resplendent quetzal (rare at this elevation). Visit the Arenal Volcano National Park visitor center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided whitewater rafting experience on the Sarapiquí or Toro River — Class III–IV rapids offering an exhilarating yet safe adventure for all levels, arranged through the resort's adventure concierge. Alternatively, explore the Arenal Hanging Bridges for a second, more leisurely self-guided crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a full volcanic hot springs evening. Private in-villa dinner option — arrange the resort's private butler dinner service on your terrace with volcano views. Or dine at Nayara's award-winning restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-villa breakfast delivered by butler service — fresh tropical fruits, eggs any style, Costa Rican tamales, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch at a riverside restaurant — grilled tilapia, rice and beans, fresh salad, and natural fruit drinks
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the resort — five-course tasting menu with local ingredients, paired with Costa Rican craft spirits and premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Whitewater rafting requires advance booking through the resort's adventure desk — confirm difficulty level preferences. The Toro River offers more challenging rapids (Class IV) while the Sarapiquí is more family-friendly (Class III). Wear quick-dry clothing for rafting. The private in-villa dinner service typically requires 24-hour advance notice.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal for Monteverde Cloud Forest — a scenic 3-hour luxury transfer through the Tilarán mountain range with stops at viewpoints overlooking Lake Arenal. Check into a luxury cloud forest lodge — recommended: El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve on a private guided walk — a less-crowded alternative to the main Monteverde reserve. Spot cloud forest specialists including quetzals, bellbirds, and dozens of orchid species. The misty, ethereal cloud forest atmosphere is unlike any other ecosystem in Costa Rica.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest — encounter nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tarantulas, glass frogs, and sleeping birds. Return to the lodge for hot chocolate and a debrief with your naturalist guide.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal resort before departure — full gourmet spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Lunch en route at a scenic mountain restaurant overlooking Lake Arenal — recommended: Tom's Pan German Bakery & Restaurant in Nuevo Arenal for European-Costa Rican fusion
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Monteverde lodge's restaurant — cloud forest-inspired cuisine featuring local dairy (Monteverde is famous for its cheese), organic vegetables, and locally sourced meats

day_by_day.notes: The road between Arenal and Monteverde is famously rough — request a 4WD luxury vehicle. Some travelers opt for a lake boat crossing + short transfer to reduce road travel. Confirm road conditions with your driver. Monteverde's cool, misty climate requires a light jacket or fleece — pack accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of Monteverde — the iconic Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges at treetop level. The experience offers breathtaking aerial views of the cloud forest and, on clear days, both Pacific and Atlantic coasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided naturalist walk — the reserve is home to over 400 bird species, 100 mammal species, and 2,500 plant species. Seek out the resplendent quetzal, one of the world's most spectacular birds, which is frequently spotted here in February during pre-nesting season.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory for a private after-hours tasting tour — Monteverde's artisan cheese tradition dates back to Quaker settlers in the 1950s. Enjoy cheese pairings with local honey, fruit preserves, and artisan crackers.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour — energy-rich options including granola, eggs, fresh fruits, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Caburé in Monteverde — renowned for its artisan chocolates and savory crepes in a cloud forest setting
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Celajes Restaurant at the Monteverde Lodge — panoramic cloud forest views, locally sourced ingredients, and an extensive Costa Rican wine and spirits list

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line canopy tour (Sky Adventures or Original Canopy Tour) well in advance — these sell out quickly, especially in February high season. Weight and health restrictions may apply for zip-lining. The quetzal is most active at dawn — consider an early morning dedicated quetzal-spotting walk before the zip-line tour. Bring a rain jacket as the cloud forest receives frequent mist and light rain.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde back to the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic mountain descent with stops at panoramic viewpoints. Stop at a local artisan market for handcrafted souvenirs — Monteverde is known for its woodwork, jewelry, and local art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort for a relaxing final beach afternoon. Indulge in the resort's full spa menu — book a signature treatment such as a volcanic mud wrap, hot stone massage, or coffee scrub using local Costa Rican coffee. Spend the late afternoon at the private beach or infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise along the Pacific coastline arranged by the resort — a private boat excursion with champagne, canapés, and front-row seats to a Pacific sunset. Spot dolphins and sea turtles en route.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure — full spread with cloud forest views
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a premium restaurant in the mountain town of Sarchí, famous for its artisan crafts — recommended: La Finca Verde for farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine
meals.dinner: Special penultimate evening dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort's finest restaurant — premium seafood tower, grilled whole lobster, and a curated dessert experience with local chocolate and tropical sorbets

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset cocktail cruise through the resort concierge in advance. The spa treatments should be reserved upon return to the resort — the most popular time slots fill quickly. The artisan market in Monteverde is best visited before departure in the morning. Request a scenic route from your driver for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the resort's private beach — a peaceful moment to reflect on 13 days of extraordinary wildlife encounters, adventures, and luxury experiences. Optional early morning yoga or meditation session offered by the resort's wellness team. Leisurely final gourmet breakfast at the ocean-view terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute resort amenities — final swim in the infinity pool, a farewell cocktail at the beach bar, and any remaining spa treatments. Complete packing and check-out formalities with the resort's concierge team. Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport arranged with ample time for international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure — concierge arranges premium lounge access at the airport. Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanoes, wildlife, and pristine Pacific beaches.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full gourmet experience one final time, with fresh tropical fruits, artisan pastries, gallo pinto, and the finest Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge — fresh ceviche, tropical fruit, and a final Imperial beer or guaro sour as a Costa Rican send-off
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with the resort concierge the night before — allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure. Juan Santamaría Airport recommends arriving 3 hours early for international flights. Request a premium airport lounge pass through your airline or credit card. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no purchasing products made from endangered species. Consider leaving a review for your exceptional naturalist guides and lodge staff.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
